title: Parallel streams, a depth step, streaming convolution, and turn-taking
brief: Lay out Moshi's time-aligned text and audio streams with their delays, interleave text and speech tokens, score and sample an RQ-Transformer's frames, stream a causal convolution chunk by chunk, and run a voice agent's turn-taking state machine against its latency budget.
hints: inner_monologue: fill the whole stream with PAD, write each word's tokens, and only then write EPAD into the frame before each word's start if no token already sits there.
delay_streams: allocate a (K, T + max(delays)) array full of pad and copy stream k into columns delays[k] to delays[k] + T.
frame_log_prob: call depth_fn once per codebook with the prefix frame_codes[:k], and add log_softmax(logits)[frame_codes[k]].
sequence_log_prob: the context for frame s is temporal_fn(codes[:s]), which sees only earlier frames; that slice is what makes the model causal.
StreamingConv1d.step: prepend the stored state to the chunk, run the same sum as causal_conv1d on that padded window, and keep the last (K - 1) * dilation input samples as the new state.
turn_taking: update the speech and silence run lengths first on every frame, then apply exactly one transition for the current state.
